traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 283 Chenopodiaceae and 284 Amaranthaceae, which APG joins as Amaranthaceae: annual or perennial herbs, some undershrubs and shrubs (saltbushes, Salsola); leaves alternate, sometimes opposite, simple; no stipules; flowers small, regular, often green, in spikes, heads or racemes among dry bracts; a calyx of 3 to 5 lobes, often dry, and no petals, read here as one whorl of tepals; ovary superior, of one cell with one ovule; fruit a one-seeded nut that stays shut (read as an achene) or opens by a lid.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Amaranthaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Chenopodiaceae, Dysphaniaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded usually no rosette, rarely a basal rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.
